topic: Dot Products and Duality: The Geometry of Measurement

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Projection Intuition
sections.content: Briefly define the dot product (a · b = |a||b|cosθ) as a measure of how much two vectors 'align.' Visualize vector 'a' casting a shadow onto vector 'b'.
sections.example: A flashlight shining on a tilted mirror; the intensity of the light hitting the surface depends on the angle of incidence.

sections.title: Defining Duality: The Linear Functional
sections.content: Introduce a vector not as an arrow, but as a 'machine.' A dual vector (covector) acts on a standard vector to output a scalar. Show the dot product as the mechanism of this machine.
sections.example: Imagine a 'filter' mask. When you pass a vector through the mask (dot product), it outputs a number (a score) representing the vector's alignment with the mask's orientation.

sections.title: Visualizing Duality via Level Sets
sections.content: Explain that a fixed covector w(v) = c defines a set of parallel lines (or hyperplanes) in 2D space. The dot product measures how many of these lines a vector crosses.
sections.example: A hiker walking across a topographical map. The covector is the 'slope direction,' and the dot product tells you how much elevation you gain.

sections.title: Synthesis: Why Duality Matters
sections.content: Conclude that dot products allow us to swap between 'points' (vectors) and 'rules' (dual vectors). This symmetry is foundational for physics (work/energy) and machine learning (SVMs).
sections.example: A 'Robot Sentry': The sentry defines a line (dual vector); any intruder (vector) that crosses the threshold (dot product > 0) triggers an alarm.
